claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is coarse-grained, single-phase, and contains no secondary dispersoids.
Adding less than 1 wt% oxide nanoparticles such as nano-Al2O3 will promote dynamic grain refinement at the CoCrFeNi sliding interface.
The oxide nanoparticles will promote formation of a self-lubricating nanocrystalline glaze layer during sliding.
The nanoparticle-modified CoCrFeNi alloy will maintain low friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
High contact stress and frictional heating, assisted by dispersed oxide nanoparticles, cause localized grain subdivision or dynamic amorphization.
Localized grain subdivision or dynamic amorphization suppresses dislocation-driven plasticity.
A shear-refined nanocrystalline surface can undergo dynamic softening and reduced shear strength.
A nanocrystalline glaze layer limits adhesive and oxidative wear.
The glaze in the proposed CoCrFeNi system is a tribochemically formed oxide layer.
The modified alloy will exhibit a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.2–0.3 across the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The modified alloy will have a wear rate at least one order of magnitude below that of baseline CoCrFeNi throughout the entire temperature range.
Untreated CoCrFeNi tends to have higher friction and wear than the proposed nanoparticle-modified material.
The baseline's poorer behavior is partly caused by less effective dynamic grain refinement and unstable surface oxide films.

The intervention is effective only when frictional heating is sufficient to activate dynamic microstructural evolution, particularly at moderate-to-high loads and sliding speeds in oxidizing environments.
The intervention's effectiveness may decrease in vacuum or highly reducing atmospheres.

contradictions.description: The mediator is described as nanocrystalline, whereas the mechanism parenthetically equates grain subdivision with dynamic amorphization. Nanocrystalline and amorphous structures are distinct states, so the proposed interfacial structure is internally inconsistent.

The hypothesis and predicted outcome claim performance across the entire temperature range under variable loads, while the boundary restricts effectiveness to conditions with sufficient frictional heating and moderate-to-high loads and speeds. Thus, performance at low load or speed within the stated test domain is both implied and excluded.
